briefs.headline: Manchester United sack Carrick and move to hire Pochettino from the USMNT
briefs.summary: Manchester United confirmed Thursday morning that Michael Carrick has departed as men's first-team head coach, after he met chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox at Carrington following their Wednesday meeting with Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco; the club statement said it intends to appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible, and ESPN reported, citing sources, that United are close to an agreement with U.S. men's national team coach Mauricio Pochettino, have made contact with U.S. Soccer ahead of triggering his $10 million release clause, and would pay about $2 million more for his staff, including assistant Jesus Perez. Carrick, 45, who signed a two-year contract in May after winning 12 of 17 matches to finish third last season, leaves with United 18th in the Premier League on one league win all season and three wins in 15 matches in all competitions, his last match a home draw with Aston Villa in which United twice came back from two goals down; sources told ESPN that U.S. Soccer expects Pochettino to oversee both Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal legs against Haiti, Saturday in Miami at 4:30 p.m. ET and Tuesday in Cincinnati at 7 p.m. ET, and United's next match is at Anfield on Nov. 22.

briefs.headline: Taylor says the Bengals' collapsed Ebiketie trade was on their end
briefs.summary: Zac Taylor said Wednesday, reading a statement he said de facto general manager Duke Tobin asked him to deliver, that the Bengals' effort to add depth for the injured Cashius Howell became more costly than anticipated, that Tobin is apologetic, that Philadelphia was a great trade partner and that the failure was on Cincinnati's end; ESPN reported, citing a source, that the agreed sixth-round-pick deal for edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie came apart when it became clear the Bengals would forfeit a 2027 compensatory third-round pick, awarded largely for losing Trey Hendrickson in free agency. Taylor said he did not ask Tobin how the club learned of the forfeiture, that it took three minutes of his day, and that Howell, placed on injured reserve Nov. 3 with a right wrist injury, is not ruled out for the season; the Bengals, with six wins and two losses, their best start in Taylor's eight seasons, host Pittsburgh on Sunday night at 8:20 p.m. ET with sole possession of first place in the AFC North going to the winner.

briefs.headline: Monken says Watson starts over Sanders on the 'full body of work'
briefs.summary: Todd Monken said Wednesday that his intention all along was to keep Deshaun Watson as the starter, that the Browns' announcement that morning of Watson as the starting quarterback for Sunday's 1 p.m. ET home game against Houston, his former team, rested on his full body of work this season, and that Monday's non-answer came only because he had not yet met with his offensive staff; Watson, who missed the New Orleans game in the concussion protocol, has five wins and three losses as a starter with five game-winning drives but a 40.9 QBR that ranks 28th of 31 qualifiers, and Shedeur Sanders went 19 of 31 for 297 yards and two touchdowns in his place in the overtime loss at the Saints. Watson said there was no question in his mind that he would remain the starter, that the rest of the season is up to Monken and the front office, and that facing Houston, where he played his first four seasons before the 2022 trade, is in the past.

briefs.headline: Spurs rally from 22 down to beat the Bulls 124-119 for a 10th straight win
briefs.summary: Victor Wembanyama scored 32 points on 13-of-18 shooting with nine rebounds and five blocks, Dylan Harper had 18 points, 10 assists and four steals and De'Aaron Fox 17 points and nine assists as San Antonio closed a four-game road trip unbeaten at the United Center on Wednesday night, two days after Wembanyama's 40 at Phoenix; Chicago scored 41 in the first quarter, started 10 of 12 from 3-point range and led 64 to 42 midway through the second, its largest lead of the season, before the Spurs opened the third with an 18 to 3 run fed by five Bulls turnovers and took control with an 11 to 2 run in the fourth. Jalen Smith tied his career high with 23 for the Bulls, who have lost eight straight, and first-round pick Caleb Wilson left in the third quarter with a right hand injury; Devin Vassell sat a second straight game with adductor tightness, and the Spurs, with 10 wins and two losses, host Golden State on Friday at 9:30 p.m. ET in NBA Cup group play, with Stephen Curry, who left Houston's win over the Warriors in the first quarter for an MRI on his right abdomen, in doubt.

briefs.headline: Fujiseiun takes a first kinboshi as Hoshoryu loses a 3rd straight bout
briefs.summary: Maegashira (rank-and-file) 2 Fujiseiun, 28, got his favored right-hand inside grip off the tachiai (initial charge), denied yokozuna (grand champion) Hoshoryu any hold on his belt and forced him out on day 5 at the Fukuoka Kokusai Center on Thursday for his first kinboshi (gold star, a rank-and-filer's win over a yokozuna), a day after losing his first bout against a yokozuna to Onosato; Hoshoryu, 27, back from three tournaments out after right knee surgery, has given up a kinboshi on three straight days, to Fujiryoga, Ura and Fujiseiun, which Kyodo said he last did at the 2025 Nagoya basho (tournament), and has two wins and three losses after opening with two wins. Japan Sumo Association chairman Hakkaku said the yokozuna's legs had no strength in them, that consecutive losses are tough and that a yokozuna has to rebuild himself and always go forward; chief judge Kokonoe, the former ozeki (champion) Chiyotaikai, said Hoshoryu's sumo looked brittle bout by bout, that the knee did not look bad, and that he wants the kihaku issen (a flash of fighting spirit) Hoshoryu pledged at his promotion. Fujiseiun, who went from Meiji University to a corporate job before turning to sumo during the pandemic and reached the top division in March, said his mind went blank at the win and that he had felt frustration, not congratulation, when his younger stablemate Fujiryoga took his own first kinboshi on day 3.

briefs.headline: Atamifuji alone unbeaten after 5 days as Onosato slaps down Ura and the ozeki all win
briefs.summary: Sekiwake Atamifuji, 24, at 198 kilograms 73 heavier than fellow sekiwake Fujinokawa, stood up slowly at the tachiai (initial charge), caught Fujinokawa's sidestep and attempted leg grab, locked him up from the left and forced him down for a fifth win in five bouts, the only unbeaten record in the top division; NHK analyst Kotokaze said Atamifuji had expected a trick and Fujinokawa's hand never reached the leg, and Fujinokawa has one win and four losses. Yokozuna (grand champion) Onosato, chasing a second straight yusho (championship), met Ura's low charge with a two-handed thrust and slapped him down by hatakikomi for his fourth win, a day after Ura beat Hoshoryu, and Kotokaze said winning by pulling is a habit the body remembers; the three ozeki (champions) all won, per Kyodo, Kotozakura forcing out Takayasu for a fourth win, Kirishima forcing out Asanoyama to stay at one loss and Aonishiki throwing Hakunofuji by shitatenage (underarm throw) for a third win. Eleven wrestlers, Onosato among them, sit one win behind Atamifuji after five days, per Nikkan Sports; day 6 is Friday in Fukuoka, and the basho (tournament) closes Nov. 22.

briefs.headline: Curry leaves for an MRI on his abdomen as the Rockets end the Warriors' 8-game run
briefs.summary: Stephen Curry grabbed at his right side minutes into Wednesday's game in Houston, yelled in pain after making a 28-foot 3-pointer with 7:22 left in the first quarter, went to the locker room and was ruled out with right abdominal soreness, then left the arena in the second half for an MRI on his abdomen and oblique; coach Steve Kerr said Curry told him he had not felt the injury before, that concern is high and that he has no idea of the extent. Kevin Durant scored 20, Alperen Sengun and Amen Thompson 19 each and Reed Sheppard hit back-to-back 3s in a fourth-quarter eight-point run as Houston won 115-108 to end Golden State's eight-game winning streak, its longest since 2022, with rookie Yaxel Lendeborg's 25 points and 10 rebounds leading the Warriors; Houston's Marcus Smart was ejected with a flagrant 2 late in the third for punching Charles Bassey. The Warriors, with eight wins and four losses, play at San Antonio on Friday.

briefs.headline: Lakers win a 7th straight at Milwaukee but lose Reaves to a heel injury
briefs.summary: Luka Doncic scored 32, Sandro Mamukelashvili 23 against the team that drafted him and Austin Reaves 18 in 25 minutes as Los Angeles won 123-112 at the Bucks on Wednesday for a league-best 11 wins against two losses, scoring 28 points off 19 Milwaukee turnovers and outscoring the Bucks 33 to 23 in the third; Reaves landed awkwardly on a missed fast-break dunk, subbed himself out with 5:20 left in the third and limped off, and coach JJ Redick said X-rays on his left heel were negative, that the Achilles is not a concern and that imaging follows Thursday in Los Angeles. Doncic turned his right ankle on a Kyle Kuzma foul with 4:25 left and said he will be fine, Collin Sexton needed stitches over his right eye after a head-to-head collision, and the Lakers do not play again until Sunday at Phoenix; Milwaukee has lost eight straight and has one win in 12 games.

briefs.headline: Celtics overcome a 22-point deficit to beat the Raptors 98-93 for a 5th straight
briefs.summary: Jayson Tatum made the tying and go-ahead free throws with 25.2 seconds left and scored 24 on 6-of-21 shooting, 10 of 12 at the line, as Boston came back from 59 to 37 down with 5:24 left in the second quarter in Toronto on Wednesday, answering with 16 straight points, the first 10 by Tatum, to trail by seven at the half; Derrick White scored 19, Payton Pritchard 14 and Neemias Queta had 11 points and 13 rebounds with Paul George sitting out ill a night after his 36 in Philadelphia. Ja'Kobe Walter, who scored 17, had 12 from 3-point range in a first quarter in which the Raptors tied a franchise record with 10 3s, going 10 of 18 from distance and then 6 of 25 the rest of the way; Toronto, without Kawhi Leonard for a ninth straight game and Scottie Barnes for a third, is below .500 for the first time this season, and Boston, with 10 wins and two losses, leads the East by a game over Philadelphia.

briefs.headline: Broncos say the deadline trade for Chargers linebacker Henley will not be finalized
briefs.summary: Denver announced late Wednesday that its trade for Daiyan Henley, agreed just before Tuesday's deadline for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder and announced as pending a physical, will not be finalized, and gave no reason; team sources told ESPN that Henley was at the Broncos' complex Wednesday and underwent a physical, and the Chargers posted a welcome back to a player who has started 41 of 42 games over three seasons and leads them with 51 tackles. Henley, 27 next week and a free agent after the season, would have gone from the winless Chargers to the first-place Broncos, who have won five straight, rank 23rd against the run and have had Alex Singleton on the field for 617 of 618 defensive snaps; it is the second deadline deal to come apart in two days after the Bengals' Ebiketie trade, and Denver, on its bye, next plays Nov. 22 against Las Vegas.

briefs.headline: Misiorowski and Schlittler sweep the Cy Young votes in their first full seasons
briefs.summary: Jacob Misiorowski, 24, took all 30 first-place votes for the National League award on Wednesday after 16 wins and five losses with a 1.80 ERA, 0.80 WHIP and 252 strikeouts in 174 2/3 innings for the World Series champion Brewers, leading the majors in all three, a 232 ERA+ that is the best full season since Pedro Martinez's 291 in 2000, a fastball averaging 100.6 mph and more than 1,000 pitches at 100 or faster; he is the first pitcher since Randy Johnson in 2001 to win the Cy Young and the World Series in the same year, and finished ahead of Philadelphia's Cristopher Sanchez and Atlanta's Chris Sale. Cam Schlittler of the Yankees swept the American League vote ahead of Toronto's Dylan Cease and Cleveland's Parker Messick, and the writers' first Reliever of the Year awards went unanimously to San Diego's Mason Miller, 1.67 ERA, 38 saves and 129 strikeouts in 70 innings, and to Toronto's Louis Varland, whose 1.27 ERA over 78 innings was the lowest among qualified relievers, with 16 of 30 first-place votes.

briefs.headline: Kucherov's third-period natural hat trick carries the Lightning past the Sabres 8-3
briefs.summary: Nikita Kucherov, who requested a trade Oct. 30, scored three straight goals and added an assist, all in the third period, after Buffalo had scored three in a row to get within a goal 33 seconds into the period on Tage Thompson's goal, and Tampa Bay won 8-3 in Buffalo on Wednesday for a fourth win in five games; John Carlson had a goal and four assists, Jake Guentzel four assists, Brandon Hagel two goals and Andrei Vasilevskiy 28 saves, while Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen was pulled after nine saves on 14 shots. In Edmonton, Evan Bouchard's one-timer 47 seconds into overtime won it 3-2 over Philadelphia, his 11th goal, most among NHL defensemen, and Connor McDavid's second-period assist extended his season-opening points streak to 20 games, tying his career high, with a league-leading 49 points; Zach Hyman scored twice and the Oilers matched the second-best 20-game start in franchise history.

briefs.headline: Toledo shuts out Massachusetts 24-0 and 4 MAC teams share the lead
briefs.summary: Connor Walendzak, in his first game this month after an undisclosed injury, capped a 90-yard drive with a 69-yard touchdown run and finished with 117 yards on 14 carries, Nicholas Thompson returned a Logan Inagawa interception 62 yards for a score, and the Rockets led 24-0 at the half and held the Minutemen to 188 yards with three sacks and 10 tackles for loss in Toledo on Wednesday night; John Alan Richter threw for 197 yards and Toledo ran for 239. Toledo, Western Michigan, Buffalo and Ohio are all 5-1 in the conference after Buffalo's 28-7 win over Ball State on Wednesday, its fifth straight; Toledo, with eight wins and two losses, hosts Bowling Green on Nov. 20, and Ohio hosts Ball State on Tuesday at 7 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: NC State moves to hire Philip Rivers, with trustees set to vote Friday
briefs.summary: The NC State board of trustees is expected to finalize a contract Friday making Philip Rivers, 44, the Wolfpack's head football coach, sources told ESPN on Wednesday; Rivers, who has never coached in college, is in his sixth season at St. Michael Catholic High School in Fairhope, Alabama, a program he built from the ground up and took to state semifinals in 2024 and 2025, and had told NC State he wanted to finish the high school season, which ended last Friday. Rivers threw for 13,484 yards and 95 touchdowns at NC State from 2000 to 2003 under Chuck Amato, who died last month at 80, played 17 NFL seasons, all but one with the Chargers, came out of retirement to start three games for the Colts last year and withdrew from the Bills' coaching search in January; his son Gunner committed to NC State in February, and Russell Wilson was also in discussions for the job after Dave Doeren was fired Oct. 24.

prime.item: Day 6 of 9. The duck table's second segment opened Saturday, Nov. 7, and closes Sunday, Nov. 15, three days out, with the third segment Dec. 21 through Jan. 31; the first, Oct. 3 to 11, is closed, and both youth waterfowl days, Sept. 19 and Oct. 31, are past. The migratory summary's duck line reads daily bag six, possession 18, with the sub-limits in footnote (c): no more than four mallards, two of them hens, two black ducks, three pintails, three wood ducks, two redheads, two canvasbacks and four sea ducks, no more than three scoters and three long-tailed ducks among them; scaup, inside the duck bag, reads one per day Nov. 7 to 15 and Dec. 21 to Jan. 11 and two per day Jan. 12 to 31; coots run the same dates as ducks at 15 and 45, mergansers the same dates at five and 15 in aggregate. Canada and white-fronted geese and snow and blue geese share the Nov. 7 to 15 segment and a third Dec. 8 through Jan. 31, daily bag five and possession 15 in aggregate; brant open Jan. 2 at one and three. Shooting hours for waterfowl are one-half hour before sunrise to sunset, and HIP registration is required. The dates are not in the hunting and trapping pamphlet, which says so itself; they are from WVDNR's separate Migratory Bird Hunting Regulations Summary 2026-2027, which fetched through the proxy at 5:45 a.m. (HTTP 200, 1,940,942 bytes, md5 aad32d21343547146e3977a821a39355, byte-identical to Wednesday's copy, a 27th straight morning).

prime.item: Day 11 of 14. waters.reading: 42.0 cfs, 1.23 feet at 5:15 a.m., falling on flow against 45.3 cfs and steady on stage against 1.26 feet in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.working: Against Wednesday's edition reading of 43.1 cfs and 1.24 feet at 5:15 a.m. the gauge is down 1.1 cfs and 0.01 feet on the day, one more step of the recession: the USGS record held 43.1 from 5 a.m. Wednesday to 9:30, traded 42.0 and 43.1 through the daylight hours, settled at 42.0 from 6:15 p.m., touched 40.9 twice overnight, at 1:30 and 2 a.m., and has read 42.0 since 3:30 a.m.; the stage went 1.24, 1.23, 1.22, 1.23 on the same steps. The fetcher's 24-hour comparison figures, 45.3 and 1.26, are Tuesday morning's values, a 48-hour window, so the day's true change is the 1.1 cfs above. At 42.0 the Williams is at the lowest reading of the fall for a fifth straight morning, under Wednesday's 43.1, Tuesday's 45.3, Monday's 48.8 and Sunday's 52.4, on a slide this paper has recorded from 1,360 cfs on Oct. 15 through 653 on Oct. 17, 141 on Oct. 24 and 70.7 on Oct. 31. The read string is the fetcher's own verdict, 42 cfs, prime wading water; the fetcher reports no water temperature for the Williams and wrote no warm-water line, so none is printed. At 42 cfs the river is a long-leader, small-fly problem, not a seam problem: the config records the Williams as a freestone trout stream of pocket water, plunge pools and undercut banks, with caddis, stoneflies and sculpin as the forage, and at this flow, the thinnest of the fall, the fish are in the plunge pools and under the cut banks, not in the pockets, which are too thin to hold them. Nine-foot or longer leaders to 6X, a size 18 to 20 caddis pupa or a small black stonefly nymph under a yarn indicator through the heads of the plunge pools and the slots between the rocks, and a size 18 to 20 dry caddis on the slow tails in the afternoon if anything is coming off; a sculpin pattern or a small olive woolly bugger swung and stripped slowly along the undercuts at first light and last light for the bigger fish, which is the one tactic that works at low water when the small flies do not. Wading is easy at 42 cfs, which is the fetcher's point, and the fish can see every step; the approach is from below and from the bank where the bank allows. No stocking line: WVDNR's trout-stocking page returned a bodiless 301 to a Bear Rock Lakes WMA notice again this morning, so nothing about fall stocking is printed.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 24.99 feet at 5 a.m., steady against 25.23 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 25.0 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Against Wednesday's edition reading of 25.02 at 5 a.m. the pool is down 0.03 on the day, and the day was the same round trip as Monday's and Tuesday's: the trace fell from 25.02 at 5 a.m. Wednesday through 24.90 at 7:30, 24.81 at 9, 24.72 at 11:30 and 24.68 at 12:45 p.m. to a low of 24.65 at 1:30 p.m., held between 24.66 and 24.76 through the afternoon with a single 24.90 reading at 5:15, then turned up through 24.80 at 6:45, 24.85 at 9:45, 24.90 at 11:30, 24.94 at 1 a.m. Thursday and 25.00 at 3:30 to 25.02 at 3:45, and read 24.99 at 5 a.m. Three days running the pool has drained a third of a foot through the daylight hours and refilled overnight, with the Williams falling all day and neither trace saying rain; whether that is the dam's holding pattern or water from upstream the gauge does not say and this paper does not guess. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, 25.0 feet, normal pool, ordinary bank access, and at 25.0 the gauge is two feet under the up-and-pushing line at 27. A normal pool that has not moved a tenth in three mornings fishes structure, which is the config's note for this reach: wing dams, riprap, the lock wall and barge cuts, with shad, skipjack and crawfish as the forage. A white or shad-pattern swimbait on a half-ounce head or a three-eighths-ounce white spinnerbait slow-rolled down the downstream face of the wing dams for hybrids and sauger, which hold where the current breaks around the dams at normal pool; a jig and minnow or a three-inch curly tail on a quarter-ounce head bounced down the riprap for sauger, and a crawfish-pattern jig crawled along the rock for the smallmouth that use the same riprap; cut shad or skipjack on a slip-sinker rig on the flats below the creek mouths and along the edges of the barge cuts for channel and flathead cats. Access at ordinary bank level at the Point Pleasant riverfront.
waters.source: USGS 03201500 (Ohio River at Point Pleasant); config.SPORTSMAN_WATERS

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 25.9 feet at 5 a.m., falling against 26.28 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 25.9 ft and falling — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Against Wednesday's edition reading of 26.03 at 5 a.m. the gauge is down 0.13 on the day, with the afternoon dip arriving later than it did Monday and Tuesday: the trace climbed from 26.03 at 5 a.m. Wednesday through 26.16 at 6:45 and 26.22 at 9:45 to a top of 26.26 at noon, held between 26.11 and 26.25 through the afternoon, fell from 26.13 at 5 p.m. through 26.04 at 5:45, 26.00 at 8:15 and 25.91 at 8:45 to the 25.9s overnight, touched 25.71 for a single reading at 1:30 a.m. Thursday, recovered to 26.04 at 2:30, and has read between 25.90 and 25.98 since 3 a.m., 25.90 at 5. The Greenup discharge record at Ironton, which this paper has used to explain the Huntington swings, was not read this morning; the shape of the trace, a half-foot swing inside the day with no rain in the basin, is the same lock-and-dam breathing the paper has recorded all week. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, 25.9 feet and falling, normal pool, ordinary bank access. This is the gauge below the dam, not the tailwater: USGS does not gauge the Ohio at Byrd, and the Corps' tailwater page serves a certificate this pipeline will not accept, so the paper prints the two gauges that bracket the dam and says which is which. At 25.9 and falling by a tenth, the Huntington reach fishes the same structure as the pool above, the config's wing dams, riprap, lock wall and barge cuts, with shad, skipjack and crawfish the forage: a white swimbait or a blade bait vertically jigged in the eddies off the lock wall and in the current seams below the dam for sauger and hybrids, a jig and minnow along the riprap, and a crawfish-pattern jig on the rock for smallmouth; cut shad or skipjack on the bottom at the creek mouths and barge cuts for channel and flathead cats. Access at ordinary bank level.

waters.reading: Sound at Hampstead: low 3:39 AM at 0.5 ft, high 9:56 AM at 4.0 ft, low 4:28 PM at 0.8 ft, high 10:10 PM at 3.0 ft. Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: low 2:14 AM at 0.6 ft, high 8:54 AM at 5.1 ft, low 3:26 PM at 0.7 ft, high 9:12 PM at 3.5 ft. Water 66.2F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, observed 5:30 a.m. Moon waxing crescent, 7% illuminated, 2.5 days old.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 9:56 AM and 10:10 PM in the sound.
waters.working: All four of the sound's events land inside the calendar day, the 3:39 a.m. low behind us at press time, and so do the surf's, the 2:14 a.m. low at Ocean City Beach pier having come an hour and 25 minutes ahead of the sound's; the sound lags the surf 62 minutes on the morning high, 62 on the afternoon low and 58 on the evening high, a flatter lag pattern than Wednesday's. The whole table is 37 to 43 minutes later than Wednesday's, and the ranges keep coming off the top of the cycle: a 3.5-foot fill overnight from 0.5 to this morning's 4.0, a tenth under Wednesday's 4.1, a 3.2-foot drain to 4:28 p.m., a 2.2-foot fill to the 10:10 p.m. high, which at 3.0 feet is the lowest evening high of the week. The moon is a waxing crescent at 7 percent, two and a half days past the new moon, so the spring tides are easing toward the first quarter: the ebb through the inlet is still strong but the extremes are softening by a tenth a day, which is a fishing fact, not decoration. NWS Wilmington has a Small Craft Advisory for the coastal waters from Surf City to Cape Fear out 20 nautical miles from 10 a.m. Thursday to 1 a.m. Friday, west winds 15 to 25 knots gusting to 30, issued at 1:03 a.m.; a west wind is an offshore wind at Topsail, blowing off the land across the sound toward the beach. No beach hazards or rip current statement is in effect for the Topsail zone this morning. The Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry report for November, published Nov. 1 and 11 days old this morning, read via WebFetch because the site blocks curl, is a monthly report and is not today's conditions: East Coast Sports has the wind producing 32-inch-plus red drum from the piers on the north end, king mackerel in double digits a day off the piers before the blow, smaller reds and the odd speckled trout in the sound with trout expected to take over as it cools; Native Son has the cooling water pushing trout to the 5- to 8-foot seams of the main creeks, reds scattered inside on cut bait, Spanish to 4 pounds in October and false albacore due; Speckled Specialist has plenty of smaller trout with some to 28 inches on live shrimp under a floating cork in 4 to 16 feet, most in 4 to 8, 3/16-ounce jig heads with a Slick Jr. for artificials, and black drum and small reds on the same shrimp over structure; Carolina Flats has topwater early to locate trout then the deeper holes, and reds on oyster and grass banks on Gulp soft plastics; Jolly Roger Pier has scattered speckled trout, Virginia mullet and spot on the bottom at night and thick bluefish early; Surf City Pier has pompano, black drum and croaker on the bottom, casting shots at Spanish and bluefish, and kings that may not be finished. On today's table the trout bite is the moving water of the morning flood into the 9:56 a.m. high, topwater at first light and then live shrimp under a cork over the oyster bars and in the 4- to 8-foot holes of the creek channels on the first of the ebb; with the water at Beaufort holding at 66.2F the trout stay in the deeper holes through the afternoon low. Red drum want the last of the fall, which on this table is roughly 1:45 to the 4:28 p.m. low, cut menhaden or a finger mullet on a quarter-ounce head a couple of feet off the creek-channel edges as the grass drains; the 10:10 p.m. high is the softest of the week at 3.0 feet, so the flooded-grass window for a weedless gold spoon is shorter tonight, and the ebb that follows runs under the dock lights toward Friday's pre-dawn low, the report's small plastics or a suspending twitchbait where the shrimp and finger mullet stack. Spot and sea mullet on bloodworm or shrimp on a two-hook bottom rig in the ICWW channel an hour either side of the evening high. Bluefish are the early-morning fish on the beach behind the bait pods on a metal jig or topwater, per both piers. Flounder are release only.
